Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are the redlines our legal and procurement teams are proposing to the MSA and Exhibit A (SOW). High level items we flagged:

- Pricing corridor language (Section 4.2) — we need a guardrail so late-stage ramp doesn't trigger outsized step-ups; proposed an annualized cap.
- Effort allocation / acceptance criteria (Exhibit A) — ambiguous deliverable definitions could create scope drift.
- Transition / ramp schedule — we expect a staged ramp (month 1–3) with clear throughput acceptance checks.

Can you confirm who on Redwood will own the first-pass counter and whether you can accept an electronic signature workflow? We are aiming to get legal terms wrapped by end of next week to align with our procurement cycle.

Subject: Re: VantagePay MSA — proposed redlines (tracking)

Karthik / Jordan — initial read and next steps below. I am attaching our tracked-changes counter (Redwood_counter_redlines_20270411.docx). Primary points:

1) Pricing corridor (Section 4.2) — vendor edits seek an open-ended uplift tied to utilization bands. We should propose a symmetric corridor with a quarterly true-up and a hard cap tied to the order form fee schedule (language included in the attached). Rationale: prevents retroactive step-ups and keeps procurement shielded from runaway billing during pilot.

2) Effort & acceptance (Exhibit A) — VantagePay's Exhibit A has a single line item for "implementation effort." We propose splitting into: onboarding (fixed milestone fee), validation acceptance tests (clear pass/fail criteria), and ongoing tuning hours (time & materials or prepaid blocks). This reduces ambiguity and aligns with our operational playbook.

3) Ramp schedule / credits — ask VantagePay to enumerate throughput thresholds per month for months 1–3. If thresholds are missed, we propose a remediation plan with limited credits (not retroactive refunds).

4) Signature / workflow — DocuSign is fine on our end. We should produce a clean order form that mirrors the fee table in the attached so procurement can sign quickly.

Jordan — please confirm whether the proposed symmetric corridor materially changes revenue recognition or introduces billing configuration work. If yes, we call that out so sales ops can estimate billing effort.

Mia — could you confirm the desired month-by-month ramp numbers (tokens/day or equivalent) and whether your legal team wants any additional audit or security language? We want to minimize back-and-forth.

Attachments: Redwood_counter_redlines_20270411.docx
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Thanks — Naomi

Subject: Re: VantagePay MSA — proposed redlines (tracking)

Thanks Naomi — that read is helpful and close to what we had in mind. Quick answers: 

- Ramp targets (tokens/day equivalent): Month 1 = 50k, Month 2 = 150k, Month 3 = 400k. These are the metrics our SRE team will use for acceptance.
- Audit/security: we only need the standard SOC2 attestation clause in the schedule; no extra controls beyond what we already reviewed.
- Signature: DocuSign acceptable. Procurement asks for a clean order form that matches the fee table in Redwood's counter and a one-page summary of acceptance criteria.

We can do a 30-minute call Thursday 4/14 at 10:00am PT to walk the Exhibit A changes and the pricing corridor language. If you can provide the clean order form and a PDF of the counter redlines before the call, we can target a sign-by date of 4/21.

Thanks — Mia
